title: SR-Scientist: Scientific Equation Discovery With Agentic AI
claim: An autonomous agent iteratively analyzes data, writes and evaluates candidate solutions with code tools, and reuses its best past attempts via memory.
layout: Single panel, top-to-bottom chat trace with side memory loop feeding back
description: A single rounded gray panel shows a vertical, top-to-bottom transcript of an agent working. A tall green arrow on the left is labeled 'Long-horizon Optimization'. At the top, a user icon and a yellow speech box give the goal: optimize the equation until the error is below 0.1%, followed by 'Previously Explored Equations'. Below, a scientist-with-microscope icon issues green thought bubbles ('First explore data', 'We can start simple...') and gray code blocks in syntax-highlighted Python. Black terminal icons mark the interpreter outputs, such as the first five data rows and a 12234% error. On the right, an 'Experience Buffer' table lists Eq/S pairs in green and yellow cells. An 'Update' arrow leads into the buffer, and a 'Fetch Top-K Equations' arrow loops back to the prompt.
caption: The inference framework of SR-SCIENTIST. At each iteration, the LLM agent autonomously conducts long-horizon optimization using code interpreters for data analysis and equation evaluation. To overcome the context length limitations of current LLMs, we implement an experience buffer to fetch the best-performing equations for subsequent iterations. ‘Eq’ denotes the equation and ‘S’ denotes the equation score.
abstract: Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been applied to scientific equation discovery, leveraging their embedded scientific knowledge for hypothesis generation. However, current methods typically confine LLMs to the role of an equation proposer within search algorithms like genetic programming. In this paper, we present SR-Scientist, a framework that elevates the LLM from a simple equation proposer to an autonomous AI scientist that writes code to analyze data, implements the equation as code, submits it for evaluation, and optimizes the equation based on experimental feedback. Specifically, we wrap the code interpreter into a set of tools for data analysis and equation evaluation. The agent is instructed to optimize the equation by utilizing these tools over a long horizon with minimal human-defined pipelines. Empirical results show that SR-Scientist outperforms baseline methods by an absolute margin of 6% to 35% on datasets covering four science disciplines. Additionally, we demonstrate our method's robustness to noise, the generalization of the discovered equations to out-of-domain data, and their symbolic accuracy. Furthermore, we develop an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework to enhance the agent's capabilities.
